prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of GLP-1 physiology and the active incretin peptide that enabled GLP-1-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: B035 is the only candidate that all six of us placed first, and on the merits rather than on the count. It runs from hormone physiology (the incretin effect, proglucagon processing, the truncated active GLP-1(7-36) peptide) to a drug class with replicated randomized evidence on glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The mechanism has been confirmed independently for decades, and the clinical consequence is now visible at population scale. It is a physiological discovery with an unambiguous medical consequence, which suits this prize better than most of the shortlist. A three-person prize of Holst (physiology), Drucker (GLP-1 biology and receptor agonism) and Mojsov (identification of the active form) maps onto three distinct, separable steps in the discovery chain.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Credit for the active peptide form and early proglucagon work is contested and extends beyond the listed names (Habener and others), and the three-person limit excludes Lotte Bjerre Knudsen, whose liraglutide and semaglutide development turned the biology into a usable drug. A prize that stops at the discoverers can be read as ignoring the step that delivered the benefit, while one that includes Knudsen forces out a physiologist. There is also some risk that the prize reads as rewarding a commercially prominent drug class rather than the underlying physiology, and long-term safety questions are still being worked out.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranked B035 first but argued that Knudsen's industrial role would crowd the three-person limit, and that the framing (physiology versus drug development) is a matter of judgement. He placed B046 second and B014 and B010 above B050 and B024.
responses.response: I agree that Knudsen is the hardest omission, and I do not think the three-person limit makes it easy. Where I differ is that I would frame the citation around the discovery chain (GLP-1 physiology and the active peptide) rather than drug development, so the credit stays with the people whose findings opened the field. I would still accept a configuration with Knudsen in place of Mojsov if the committee finds the evidence for Mojsov's priority weaker than I do. I do not share your placement of B010 and B014 as close seconds. Both are enabling technologies whose recognition would be defensible, but neither has a disease-level outcome comparable to B029 or B012.

responses.point: El-Manira ranked B046 (optogenetics) second and B001 and B024 next, emphasizing that optogenetics is original, ubiquitous in circuit analysis and mature, and proposing Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann.
responses.response: I agree that optogenetics is original and mature, but I put it behind B029 and B012 as a prize in physiology or medicine because its impact is on the experimental toolkit and not yet on patients. The attribution problem is also more severe than for B035 or B029. Six credited people exceed the limit, and the proposed trio omits Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck, each with a strong claim. I would not rule it out, but the committee would have to accept a method prize with a contentious three-way split, and I think that makes it a weaker lead than B035.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius placed B002 (TNF blockade) third and B012 fourth, treating TNF blockade as a textbook bench-to-bedside discovery with a clean two-person configuration, and also listed B038 (IL-6).
responses.response: B002 has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and I agree it is fully mature, so I take the case seriously. My reservation is that it is a translational validation of an already-known cytokine, and the committee should ask whether the key discovery is TNF's role in disease or the later antibody engineering, which falls outside the credited names. I would place it below B029 and B012 because those two opened an entirely new modality or paradigm, but I would not object strongly if the committee preferred its clean credit. It is a reasonable second part to pair with B035 if we wanted two achievements.

responses.point: Svenningsson ranked B035 first, B029 second and B046 third, and flagged that the three-person limit forces a choice on B035 and that B029 lacks other early CAR originators such as Eshhar.
responses.response: I agree with the chair that B035 and B029 are the two strongest cases, and that B029's missing early originator (Eshhar) is a real gap, not a footnote. That gap is what separates it from B035 for me. B029 can only go forward as an imperfect trio of June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, whereas the B035 trio is separable by discovery step. I would keep B029 as my first alternative, and if the committee preferred two achievements I would pair B035 with a B029 part for June and Sadelain, and I accept that this would require dropping Mojsov or Holst from the first part.

responses.point: Perlmann ranked B035, B029 and B012 as his top three, with B012 as a molecular-targeted-therapy paradigm and attribution among Druker, Lydon and Sawyers.
responses.response: I share the view that B012 is the founding example of targeted kinase therapy, and that is why it is my second alternative. I would qualify it on two points. First, the groundwork by Rowley, Nowell and Witte lies outside the credited names, which complicates the story that the prize would tell. Second, it has the longest history of earlier recognition on the list, so the question is whether a prize now adds anything to a case that has long been settled; I think it does, but the timing is less compelling than for B035.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or Knudsen should occupy the third place alongside Holst and Drucker, and how much weight the committee gives to priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide.
Whether the committee prefers a physiology-centred or drug-development-centred framing of B035, which affects both the citation and the laureate set.
Whether a two-achievement prize (B035 with B029 or B002) is preferable to a single-achievement prize given how many strong contributors would then be excluded.
Long-term safety and outcome data for GLP-1 receptor agonists are still accumulating.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for any shortlisted ballot. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén on single-cell work, but none of the shortlisted candidates is in single-cell methods or involves them, and shared affiliation with Karolinska Institutet creates no documented tie to any credited name.
